messages.subject: estimation methods cfa
parts:
Hi everyone,

I’m working with a longitudinal survey that includes a 5-item mental health scale, administered every two years to a sample of participants from 2000 to 2010. The items are measured on a 1–4 ordinal scale.

I am performing a Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) and would like to compare two estimation approaches:

- WLSMV (Weighted Least Squares Mean and Variance Adjusted), using the following code:

fit_ac <- cfa(m_ac, data = data1,
              ordered = colnames(data1[,12:104]),
              missing = "pairwise",
              estimator = "WLSMV",   std.lv = TRUE)

- PML (Pairwise Maximum Likelihood) for ordinal data. ( Pairwise likelihood estimation for factor analysis models with ordinal data - ScienceDirect)

fit <- cfa(HS.model, data = HSbinary[,1:4],
           ordered = names(HSbinary[,1:4]),
           estimator = "PML")
lavTablesFitCm(fit)
lavTablesFitCp(fit)
lavTablesFitCf(fit)

  
  I would really appreciate any feedback on the following:

  • Is it appropriate to compare results from WLSMV and PML estimation in this context (ordinal data, repeated measurements over time)?

  • Is the implementation correct for both estimators?

  • Are there specific considerations or pitfalls I should be aware of when interpreting and comparing these models?

Thanks in advance for your suggestions

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: estimation methods cfa
parts:
Sara,
     You are not going to use *exactly* this syntax, right? Because the two pieces of syntax refer to different datasets with different numbers of observed variables. Also, the first approach applies a missing data procedure, "pairwise," while the second applies no procedure, and so, I believe, lavaan would default to listwise. Different missing data procedures would confound comparisons across methods.
     You plan a comparison, but how will you judge the comparison? Do you know "correct" values for the quantities you plan to calculate? Do you have another basis for determining that one set of results is better than the other?
